{{Short description|Irish hurling tournament}} {{refimprove|date=June 2020}} {{Use Irish English|date=March 2020}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2020}} {{Infobox GAA championship |image = |name = Munster Senior Hurling Championship |county = |province = |year = 2018 |trophy = |sponsor = |date = 20 May–1 July |num_teams = 5 |defending_champions = [[Cork GAA|Cork]] |winners = [[Cork GAA|Cork]] |ordinal = 54th |manager = [[John Meyler]] |captain = [[Séamus Harnedy]] |qualify_for = [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster SHC Final]]
[[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] |runnersup = [[Clare GAA|Clare]] |runnerupmanager = [[Donal Moloney]]
[[Gerry O'Connor (hurling manager)|Gerry O'Connor]] |runnerupcaptain = [[Patrick O'Connor (hurler)|Patrick O'Connor]] |promoted = |relegated = |matches = 11 |total_scored = |poty = |topscorer = |website = |previous = [[2017 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2017]] |next = [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2019]] }} The '''2018 Munster Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 2018 installment of the annual [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] organised by [[Munster GAA]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/2017/10/2018-munster-hurling-football-championship-draws/|title=2018 Munster Hurling & Football Championship Draws|date=19 October 2017}} This was the first year of [[#Format|a new format]]. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] won a second consecutive title by defeating [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|the final]]. ==Format== A new provincial hurling championship featuring five-team round-robin groups in both Leinster and Munster and the new Joe McDonagh Cup was introduced in 2018 for an initial three-year period. The proposal was carried by a narrow margin with 62% voting in favour (a majority of at least 60% was required) at the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]]'s [[Gaelic Athletic Association Congress|Special Congress]] on 30 September 2017. The top two teams in each provincial group would contest the provincial final, with the provincial winners advancing to the All-Ireland semi-finals and the losing provincial finalists advancing to the two quarter-finals.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa-votes-to-change-senior-hurling-championship-807964.html |title=GAA votes to change senior hurling championship |date=30 September 2017|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=19 October 2017}} An amendment to the motion from [[Laois GAA|Laois]], [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Meath GAA|Meath]] was carried by 87%. The third-placed teams in Leinster and Munster would compete in All-Ireland preliminary quarter-finals against the two Joe McDonagh Cup finalists, with the Joe McDonagh Cup teams having home advantage. If a non-Munster team were to win the Joe McDonagh Cup, the bottom team in the Leinster championship would be relegated to the following year's Joe McDonagh Cup and would be replaced in the following year's Leinster championship by the Joe McDonagh Cup winners. If a Munster team were to win the Joe McDonagh Cup, they would play off against the team who finished bottom in the Munster championship for the right to play in the following year's Munster championship, thereby ensuring that only Munster teams compete in the Munster championship.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/0930/908716-hurling-championship/ |title=Historic day at Croke Park as Congress votes in hurling structure changes|date=30 September 2017|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=19 October 2017}} The restructure of hurling involved the reduction of the Leinster championship from nine teams to five while the Munster championship continued with the previous five Munster teams (Kerry previously competed in the qualifier group of the Leinster championship). A six-team [[Joe McDonagh Cup]] was created, consisting of all four teams from the 2017 Leinster qualifier group plus Antrim and Carlow, the [[2017 Christy Ring Cup]] finalists. ==Teams== The Munster championship was contested by five of the six counties from the Irish province of [[Munster]].
